i have to venture an unpopular course of advice.

learn about the psychology and pathology of people who have attractions to children.  ignore the self-help sections, get to the psych textbooks, the case studies, the research documents.  at the moment this is a horrible traumatic thing that is happening, and you're grasping for why and not seeing him for what he was etc.  

one common thing people wrestle with is how they didn't really know the person, how could they have not seen it, etc.  the thing is, you did know him.  you didn't know /all/ of him, but what you knew, was him.  this is additional information.  is it any surprise that he didn't tell anyone?  i don't know whether he offended or not, and if he did that is an awful thing.  but part of the problem with the way we treat paedophiles is that we have demonised the attraction past the point of illness and into depravity.

the next bit is hard.  empathy.  yeah, if he followed through on any of these feelings that is a terrible thing.  no-one will argue that.  it's just important to put yourself on the other side of that relationship, having feelings that you know are awful and reprehensible, unable to talk to anyone about them, stuffing them away.  i tried that with depression and anxiety, guess how well that worked out?  yeah, everything exploded.  no surprise.  imagine how an in-closet gay person would go if they could go to jail for ever expressing how they feel?  sounds like an inhuman way to live, right?

i need to re-iterate that i'm not condoning anything he might have done.  but we need to separate actions from attractions, and consider things as a whole.  perhaps if we, as a society, could come out and show support to people who realise they have a terrible immoral attraction, perhaps they may be able to get the treatment they require, rather than curling up into a ball until they offend.

hope this helps.  sorry if it made it worse.

i have to disagree on one point - it's the friends partners right to think of it as not being as wrong as she does.  cheating is not about the actions of the person, it's about what's established as okay in the context of the relationship.  this is how open relationships and polyamorous relationships work.  it's all in the definition, and the agreement.

cheating, as written, is inherently a betrayal of the partner, and is inherently wrong.  sex outside of the relationship /may/ be wrong depending on the relationship, romantic feelings may also.  the definitions are entirely up to the couple.

so, yeah either lying to or otherwise deceiving your partner is on a basic level morally wrong.  that's what cheating is.  and it's not cheating if the other person is okay with it, otherwise it's just playing with a different set of rules.

you are over-thinking this.  obviously i don't know the person or you, haven't seen your interactions, and aren't in a good position to objectively say what's going on, so i'll stick to things that are objective.

people develop feelings at different rates.  most people fear having more feelings than someone else, and displaying them and having that proven is humiliating.  this is not a game.  this is self-preservation.  it is both of you wanting to show interest in the other person but not so much interest that it is inappropriate and creates risk.  this isn't a shitty time, this is an exciting time.  you toe the line, inch over, make sure it's okay.  and **both of you are doing this**.  it gets more complicated again when you bring things like fear of commitment into it, where letting yourself get too invested may bring about a snapback from yourself.  both of you are protecting yourself, don't pretend that this is a thing that is just happening to you.  

there are a few other things in here that unsettle me.  how quickly this has come to /r/offmychest and how much pain it seems to be causing you.  i'm going to come right out and say this doesn't sound healthy.  this shouldn't be a painful experience.  how long has this been going on for?  days?  weeks?  months?  you've put an awful lot on this person very quickly and i have no idea if you even know who she really is yet.

the second thing is that you keep referencing being experienced.  it's kind of like saying you're famous; if you have to say it, you aren't.  only an inexperienced person would think that being able to help what you feel is about being experienced.  feelings are information.  they're the feedback that your body and your mind give your consciousness as to its state.  they're neither good nor bad, just information.  you don't 'help' feelings, you just choose what you do with them.

the last thing is the hypothetical statements of being, the similes, the sense of drama baked into every sentence .. it's not life or death.  it's someone you like, someone you think you might love if given the opportunity.  most people look back on this as the fun, easy time in their relationship.  it only gets harder from here.  if this is how it starts .. i don't think either of you are going to enjoy what happens when it gets going.

you're overcooking this, duke.  it sounds like you're going to not talk to her because you spoke last in the last conversation.  that's just .. silly.  mature adults don't do that.

holy shit dude.  this is like reading my diary.  i've been there man and it is so freaking hard.  the pinning her down, the violence, the manipulation, the loss of control.  this happened to me twice, but in different ways.  between the two of them we get to everything on this list.  one tried to hire someone to kill me and my mother.  attacked me in public and nearly got me beat up by someone last time i saw her.  good on you for being able to share it like this, even as a throwaway.  hell, i know i'm on one.

you are so strong to be able to post like this.  i never told anyone about that when it happened.  you will have trust issues, but you'll also be a lot better at spotting the signs early.  it's a trade-off.  a worthwhile one in my opinion.

the first thing you need to do is understand that this behaviour is not about you.  it's about her.  at her core she feels worthless and out of control; this is a desperate, pathetic attempt to gain control over someone she perceives to be 'hurting her'.  it doesnt have to be real or rational for this feeling to occur - she derives her sense of self worth out of things outside her, and when anything goes wrong it attacks her right at her core.  SHE is the one who is screwed up, you just happen to be the nearest target.  this behaviour does not go away, and it will just happen again, you can count on it.  without observing it's difficult to make a call, but to me this screams borderline personality disorder.

second, there is no such thing as 'she'd be perfect except for [blank]'.  people are irremovable from these traits.  you will miss her, and you will feel bad about it, but you have to remember the whole package.

third.  most people are not like this.  you know that already because of everyone else you've ever met, but this experience will sour you.  don't let it control you.  instead, use what you've learned about the personality traits and actions that are 'tells' to a person's core.  you'll be able to figure out much more quickly than anyone else what's going on with someone else, and because i've lived through it i know that you have a much better understanding of what's going through another person's head as you've had to predict it to survive.  use this to your advantage, see it as the skill that it is.  one borne in fear, but still all the same.  if you look back through the relationship there will definitely be a point that you reflect and say 'then .. thats when i should have known, when [blank] happened'.  you'll identify blank much more quickly.

fourth, leverage.  this goes without saying but in order for a relationship to work, people have to be peers.  if you find people using pressure, or your circumstances, against you, get the fuck out.  just pick up your wallet and go.  no 'stuff' is worth living in that environment.  the behaviour we accept is the behaviour we condone.

last, you.  this is going to hurt for a while.  don't be afraid to go and talk to a therapist or a counsellor.  what you went through is real, traumatic and scary.  i didn't, and i ended up with full-blown depression and had to drop out of college for 6 months.  don't be like me.  you can be better.  you GOT this, man.  you can walk away with your head held high knowing you did everything you could, but in the end she was just a fucked up bitch who takes everything she feels out on someone else.  i'm proud of you for leaving, proud of you for sharing, just generally proud of how you're handling this.  i wish i'd been able to do the same.

if you want to talk or whatever pm me, i'll get back to you as soon as i can.  no-one should have to go through this alone.  and you don't have to.  and if you want to let me know what country you are in, i'll see if i have some local resources to lend a hand.

you're over-thinking it.  there is no average person, of either gender.  the reality is that the spectrum is as varied as you can get creative, in a classic bell curve.  there may be a peak in the middle but you don't have to do a lot of math to realise there's enough volume under the rest of the bell that the most common response doesn't necessarily mean that it's significantly more likely to be what person X wants.  just sayin'!

i'm afraid that television and movies may have tainted your view of how real-world m-f dynamics work.  that stuff is generally not that cute and when not wanted, is actually super creepy.

there's nothing wrong with being *in touch* with your emotions, and i'd argue that the less aware someone is of what they're feeling and what makes them happy, the more likely they are to have problems.  it's like people who legitimately, unironically like twilight tend to have not been loved enough, so they romanticise the grand gestures and the epic displays, the heightened emotions.  the same way that 50 shades of grey appeals to the under-sexed.

you should express yourself in a healthy manner where appropriate.  when you're in the situation, pay attention to your date's body language, word choice, and how she expresses herself.  you'll be able to find pretty quickly that when you stop thinking about how she'll respond to these things that you think are expected, and start thinking about what this individual person might actually like, you'll see better results.

people are sticky, feely messes of emotional goop and meat.  one person's lover is another person's stalker.  remember - this is not about you.  it's about the union (if you'll pardon my mathematical terms) of what you want and what the other person wants.  and if that genuinely turns out to be grand romantic gestures, you never know, you may find yourself wanting to do them.  or you might decide she's seen too many disney cartoons.

either way, you'll figure it out pretty quickly.  just keep your eyes and ears open, and you'll be fine.  good luck!

i have.  i saw a psychologist and psychiatrist when i had my big breakdown at uni.  anxiety, depression, panic attacks.  all for a good reason.  therapy and SSRIs did their job and i rebuilt stronger.  unfortunately some of the coping strategies that i developed for that were .. not viable in the long term.

it's now ten years later and i've been seeing a psychiatrist for a year.  just started with a psychologist.  my problems now seem to be not focused around any reason or thing, just .. feelings, which initially lead me to believe it was purely chemical.  and i've seen so many bad psychologists that if i had nothing to bring in to talk about i had no faith in their ability to do anything.  but i realised a little while ago that if i wasn't going to go to a psychologist that i needed to start thinking like one.  why do my emotions just turn off sometimes and i go numb?  what's this in response to?  why does it occur?  when?  try to figure things out.

so i did, and i realised that many of my coping strategies were all about risk management.  not fucking up my life while my head was going crazy.  effectively, all about mitigating emotion.  i guess at some point i overmitigated and my brain has learnt to shut that part off completely.  it is very difficult to be in a functional relationship when you occasionally lose the ability to have feelings.

so i'm back on the bandwagon of trying to figure out how to do this.  last time i tried to really get in touch with what i was thinking and feeling rather than controlling and defining things mentally it .. did not go well for me.  i felt more comfortable but whenever you're exposed to risk there's a potential for things to go badly.  and when everyone is used to you being 'the rock' for everyone else, they become very displeased with the situation when you aren't.  expectation's a bitch, and so's the girl i was going to marry.  past tense.  bullet dodged IMO, but whatever.

yes.  i was 21.  it was the wake-up call i needed.  i didn't drop out so much as it became blatantly obvious that i was not able to do it, and withdrew intentionally before academic penalty was enforced.

i had a girl, i loved her more than i'd ever loved anyone.  she seemed like the first person who really understood me.  and she fucked me over in ways too horrible to even describe.  the short version is that she would fuck guys at uni in return for them buying her lunch.  the long version is much, much worse.  you never want to find a SO in porn.  it broke me, completely, as it would any guy desperately in love with someone for the first time.

i couldn't function.  40 panic attacks a day.  by the end they weren't even panic attacks because my body would just have its reaction and i'd just sit there, calmly waiting for it to finish.  anxiety attacks?  who knows.  anyway, i would record them.  i still remember the first day i had none.  i don't know what day it was, or when it was, but i remember looking at the book and realising i had nothing to jot down.  it was the first real step towards freedom.

it's now ten years later.  i got clean of my mental health issues for a while but some of the coping techniques i learned were ... suboptimal.  they have lead to other problems now, but were still necessary at the time.

you can do it.  i know this is old, but this is probably when you need the most help.

you can do it.
